references.text: God calls Moses up the mountain to give him the stone tablets with the law and commandments that God has written.
Moses comes down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony, which were written on both sides and were the work of God.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets after the first ones were broken.
Moses was on the mountain for forty days, and God wrote the Ten Commandments on the tablets.
God declared His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them on two stone tablets.
God gave Moses the two stone tablets written with God's finger, containing all the words that God had spoken on the mountain.
Moses carves out new stone tablets, and God writes the Ten Commandments on them just as on the first tablets.
Paul contrasts stone tablets written with ink with Christ's letter written by the living Spirit of God on tablets of human hearts.
Confirms that the tablets were written on both sides, emphasizing God's complete and unchangeable word.
Illustrates God's grace through the restoration of the covenant tablets after the breaking of the first set.
Moses' own confirmation in Deuteronomy strengthens the authority that God's finger wrote the words of the covenant.
Connects the giving of the law with the personal transformation of those who have met God.
Confirms the continuity of God's gift of covenant tablets even after a period of prayer and reconciliation.
